description: Application-level monitoring for Archestra platform deployments: HTTP traffic, Node.js runtime health, resource usage, task queue processing, and PostgreSQL database health

options.content:

panels.title: Scrape health (lowest target)
panels.description: Lowest Prometheus up value among the selected scrape jobs: 1 means all reported targets are up; 0 means at least one scrape failed. Some remote-write pipelines omit up, so no samples is not proof that targets are healthy.

panels.title: API requests / second
panels.description: HTTP requests handled per second across selected processes, including API and health endpoints. Use route panels below to identify which endpoints drive traffic.

panels.title: API P95 request duration
panels.description: 95th-percentile HTTP handler duration across selected processes. This is API server latency, not full model generation time.

panels.title: Request Rate
panels.description: HTTP requests per second by route and method. Health checks and monitoring requests can account for a large share of traffic.

panels.title: Request Duration
panels.description: HTTP request latency from histogram observations, grouped as shown in the legend. Inference streaming can outlive the HTTP handler's recorded duration.

panels.title: Error Rate
panels.description: HTTP responses classified as errors per second. Compare affected routes and response codes with traffic before interpreting a spike.

panels.title: Top Slowest Routes (P95)
panels.description: Routes with the highest 95th-percentile HTTP request duration. Low-volume routes can have unstable percentile estimates.

panels.title: Request Rate by Status Code
panels.description: HTTP request rate grouped by response status code. A provider failure after streaming headers may still have an HTTP 200 status; use logical proxy outcomes for those failures.

panels.title: Event Loop Lag (P50, P90, P99)
panels.description: Delay before Node.js can run scheduled work, by process and percentile. Sustained lag indicates the event loop is busy or blocked.

panels.title: GC time per second
panels.description: Seconds spent in garbage collection per elapsed second, displayed as a proportion. Sustained collection pressure can increase request latency.

panels.title: Heap Usage by Space
panels.description: Node.js heap bytes by V8 memory space. Compare sustained growth with garbage collection rather than treating every increase as a leak.

panels.title: Active Handles & Requests
panels.description: Node.js handles and requests still active in each process, such as sockets and filesystem operations. These are runtime objects, not the number of user API calls.

panels.title: Process CPU cores used
panels.description: CPU seconds consumed per elapsed second by each process. A value of 1 represents one fully used CPU core.

panels.title: Memory Usage
panels.description: Process memory in bytes, grouped by the memory category in the legend. Resident memory includes more than the JavaScript heap.

panels.title: Process Uptime
panels.description: Elapsed time since each process started. A drop indicates a restart or a different scrape target.

panels.title: Active Tasks
panels.description: Background tasks currently executing. This is task-queue work, separate from Agent Runtime task health.

panels.title: Total Enqueued
panels.description: Background tasks added during the selected period. A task can be retried later; this is not a unique user-request count.

panels.title: Total Completed
panels.description: Background tasks completed during the selected period, across selected processes.

panels.title: Dead-Lettered
panels.description: Tasks moved to the dead-letter state during the selected period after exhausting their retry policy. Inspect task failures when this rises.

panels.title: Stuck Tasks Reset
panels.description: Tasks whose stale execution claim was reset during the selected period so they could be retried. Repeated resets can indicate worker interruptions.

panels.title: Task Throughput
panels.description: Background task events per second by outcome. Compare arrivals and completions to identify accumulating work.

panels.title: Task Processing Duration (P95)
panels.description: 95th-percentile duration of background task execution, grouped as shown. This does not measure time spent waiting in the queue.

panels.title: Active Tasks Over Time
panels.description: Background tasks executing at each scrape, by task type or process. Counts describe concurrent work, not throughput.

panels.title: Failed & Dead Tasks
panels.description: Failed task attempts and dead-letter transitions per second. A retried task can contribute more than one failure.

panels.title: Active Connections
panels.description: PostgreSQL connections reported by the selected external database exporter. Requires that exporter; it is separate from the application's client pool.

panels.title: Max Connections
panels.description: PostgreSQL's configured connection ceiling from the selected database exporter. This is server capacity, not the application's pool size.

panels.title: Connection Utilization
panels.description: Reported PostgreSQL connections as a percentage of the server's configured connection ceiling. Missing exporter data remains unknown.

panels.title: WAL Size
panels.description: Write-ahead log size reported by the PostgreSQL exporter, in bytes. This panel requires database metrics outside Archestra's application scrape.
Estimated database storage utilization for Kubernetes-backed PostgreSQL. Uses summed non-system database size divided by the PostgreSQL PVC requested storage from kube-state-metrics.
panels.title: DB Size Utilization
Active Connections Over Time
panels.description: PostgreSQL connection counts over time, grouped by database or connection state as exported. Compare with the server connection ceiling.
Database sizes excluding PostgreSQL system databases. The dashed line is the inferred PostgreSQL PVC requested storage from kube-state-metrics for Kubernetes-backed deployments.
panels.title: Database Size
Transactions
panels.description: PostgreSQL transactions per second, split by commits and rollbacks. Application retries can increase transaction volume without increasing user traffic.

panels.title: Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description: Share of database block accesses served from PostgreSQL's buffer cache. This is database caching, not LLM prompt caching.

panels.title: Row Operations
panels.description: PostgreSQL row operations per second, grouped by operation. Requires database-exporter statistics.

panels.title: Locks by Mode
panels.description: PostgreSQL locks by lock mode and database. Counts alone do not prove blocking; correlate with latency and database activity.

panels.title: Deadlocks
panels.description: PostgreSQL deadlocks per second. Any sustained increase warrants investigation of conflicting transactions.

panels.title: Temp Bytes Written
panels.description: Temporary data written by PostgreSQL per second, often from sorts or hashes that spill to disk. Requires a database exporter.

panels.title: Database client pool connections
panels.description: Application-owned database connections by pool state. Idle connections remain open for reuse; waiting work can indicate pool saturation.

panels.title: Configured pool capacity
panels.description: Maximum client connections configured for each application's database pool. Each process owns its own pool.

list.name: job
list.label: Scrape job
list.description: Prometheus target group: a set of monitored processes. Leave All to include every matching source.
